assumptions.text: The integrity of American democracy depends on accessible and reliable mail-based systems, especially for voting.
Voting by mail is a legitimate and necessary mechanism for ensuring broad civic participation.
Efforts to undermine the USPS are part of a broader pattern of dismantling federal institutions aimed at weakening democratic governance.
Historical progress toward expanded suffrage should continue rather than be reversed.
Reducing voter turnout serves the interests of conservative power structures.
The idea that some citizens should not vote reflects a fundamentally undemocratic worldview.
Benjamin Franklin’s vision of a republic hinges on active citizen engagement and institutional resilience.
Social media platforms like Twitter amplify civic discourse and are effective tools for collective action.
Personal privacy is secondary to public safety and civic responsibility in the context of mail delivery.
Public trust in governmental institutions is fragile and easily eroded by intentional disinformation campaigns.
